body:
WHAT
The import graph maps which source files import which, across many languages, using regex scans (no AST). It is built the first time a GraphQuery runs and saved to `.magentra/graph.json`; later loads reuse entries whose mtime and size are unchanged. `GraphQuery blast <files>` lists every module that transitively imports them (with hop distance); `GraphQuery deps <file>` lists what a file transitively depends on. `GraphData.version` must be bumped whenever import extraction changes, because unchanged files keep their cached edges otherwise.

WHY
Without a graph the agent must read files to guess blast radius; without the version bump a scanner fix never reaches a workspace that already has a graph.json.

WHERE
engine/core/src/knowledge/graph.ts — GraphData (version: 3), GraphFileEntry, buildGraph(cwd, prev), loadOrBuildGraph(cwd), saveGraph(), isValidGraph(), graphsEqual(), blastRadius(g, files), dependencies(g, file, maxDepth), extractImports(). Called lazily per query from engine/tools/src/graphQuery.ts — execute() `loadOrBuildGraph(ctx.cwd)` and the 'blast'/'deps' ops; also engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — buildClarifySkim().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. In a temp workspace where b.ts imports a.ts and c.ts imports b.ts, blastRadius(loadOrBuildGraph(cwd), ['a.ts']) returns b.ts at distance 1 and c.ts at distance 2 and never lists a.ts itself; dependencies(g, 'c.ts') returns b.ts (1) and a.ts (2).
2. loadOrBuildGraph creates .magentra/graph.json on first call; a second call with no file changes does not rewrite the file (mtime unchanged) and returns equal data.
3. After editing a.ts to add an import of d.ts, the next loadOrBuildGraph re-extracts only a.ts (its mtime/size changed) and the new edge appears, while an untouched file's entry is reused.
4. A graph.json whose version is 2 (or corrupt JSON) is rejected by isValidGraph and a full rebuild is written with version 3.
5. Package imports produce `pkg:<name>` nodes that dependencies() lists but blastRadius() excludes from results.
